_meta.source: Hand-curated estimates (Wikivoyage 'Get around', operator and city transport sites). Ride-hailing apps change often: only apps we are fairly confident operate are listed.

taxi.tip: No Uber or Bolt. Agree on the price before you set off or insist on the meter; guesthouses can call a reliable taxi.
No Uber or Bolt. Coastal taxis cost more in summer; agree on the fare first or use a company your accommodation recommends.
Metered taxis are cheap in Sarajevo. Avoid unofficial drivers touting at bus and train stations.
Book through an app or call a company. Avoid drivers who approach you at the airport or bus station.
Taxis are cheap; make sure the meter is on.
Taxis are cheap and metered; make sure the meter is on.
Apps are usually much cheaper than street taxis, especially in Dubrovnik and Split.
Call a local taxi company; fares are metered. Public transport and walking cover most of Ljubljana.
Taxis are metered (night rate after midnight). The apps book licensed taxis.
Check the price sticker on the window before getting in: some taxis charge several times the normal rate. Use well-known companies (e.g. OK Supertrans or Yellow Taxi in Sofia).
Use Uber or Bolt; street taxis at airports and stations often overcharge.
Taxis are cheap. Ask your accommodation to book one by phone.
Uber is banned. Bolt books licensed taxis; Budapest taxi fares are regulated.
Apps are usually cheaper than taxis waiting at stations.
Use an app: street taxis in central Prague are known for overcharging tourists.
Uber and Bolt work in the big cities; in small towns, call a local taxi.
Apps are cheap and widely used; avoid unmarked taxis at stations.
Apps are the normal way to get a taxi.
Apps are the normal way to get a taxi; street taxis in Riga's old town can be pricey.
Bolt started in Tallinn and is the normal way to get a taxi.
Yandex Go is the norm. Foreign bank cards don't work, so choose cash payment in the app and pay the driver.
Apps are cheap and widely used.
Yandex Go is the norm; foreign bank cards may not work, so carry cash.
Taxis are metered and honest; most drivers speak little English, so show the address in Chinese.
Taxis are clean, metered and honest but expensive. Doors open automatically: no need to touch them.
Insist on the meter in Bangkok or use Grab/Bolt; tuk-tuk drivers quote high prices and may take you to gem shops.
Use Grab or Xanh SM. For street taxis choose Mai Linh or Vinasun, and watch for look-alike fakes.
Grab is the norm; street taxis often refuse to use the meter.
Taxis are metered, with surcharges at peak hours, late at night and from the airport.
Tuk-tuks and remorks are everywhere: agree the price first, or book in PassApp/Grab.

tirana.pay: Cash to the conductor on board (well under €1)
tirana.note: Buses have no route maps or English signs; the centre is walkable.

shkoder.note: Flat and bike-friendly; many guesthouses rent bikes.

theth.note: Mountain village: you walk. Guesthouses arrange 4x4 or minibus transfers.

berat.note: Old town is walkable but steep.

gjirokaster.note: Steep cobbled streets; take a taxi up to the castle if needed.

sarande.note: Local buses run to Ksamil and Butrint, more often in summer.

kotor.note: Buses run along the bay; the old town is car-free.

zabljak.note: Little or no local transport: taxis or hitching to trailheads.

sarajevo.pay: Tickets from kiosks (cheaper) or the driver; validate on board

belgrade.pay: Free: city public transport has been free since January 2025
belgrade.note: Google Maps shows routes and times.

peja.note: Taxis or hiking to the Rugova Gorge.

ohrid.note: Boats and taxis to lakeside sights like St. Naum.
ohrid.rentalNote: Bikes and scooters for the lakeshore road to St. Naum.

dubrovnik.pay: Ticket from kiosks or the app; buying from the driver costs more
dubrovnik.note: Old town is car-free; ferries to Lokrum and the Elaphiti islands.

split.note: Ferries and catamarans to the islands leave from the harbour by the old town.

zagreb.pay: Tickets at kiosks or in the app; from the driver costs more. Validate on board

ljubljana.note: Car-free centre; funicular up to the castle.
ljubljana.rentalNote: BicikeLJ bike share stations across the centre.

bled.note: Walk or cycle around the lake.
bled.rentalNote: Bikes are the easiest way around the lake and to Vintgar Gorge.

athens.pay: Contactless bank card on validators, or a ticket/card from machines
athens.note: Metro line 3 runs to the airport.

bucharest.pay: Contactless bank card on validators (surface transport and metro)

brasov.note: Buses to Bran and Râșnov leave from the bus station; cable car up Mount Tâmpa.

chisinau.pay: Cash to the conductor on board (very cheap)

budapest.pay: Tickets and passes in the BudapestGO app or at machines
budapest.note: Trams 2, 4 and 6 are sights in themselves; boats on the Danube are part of the network.

bratislava.pay: Contactless bank card on board, or the app

poprad.note: The Tatra Electric Railway runs from Poprad to the mountain resorts.

prague.pay: Contactless bank card at machines and on trams, or the PID Lítačka app
prague.note: Validate paper tickets; inspectors fine on the spot.

ceskykrumlov.rentalNote: Canoe and raft rental on the Vltava is popular.

brno.pay: Tap a contactless bank card on board

vienna.pay: Tickets and passes from machines or the WienMobil app
vienna.note: No barriers, but inspectors fine riders without a valid ticket; stamp paper tickets before boarding.
vienna.rentalNote: WienMobil Rad bike share across the city.

salzburg.pay: Tickets from machines, the driver or the Salzburg Verkehr app
salzburg.note: The old town is compact; the funicular goes up to the fortress.

hallstatt.note: Tiny village, best on foot; a ferry crosses the lake to the train station.

innsbruck.pay: Tickets from machines or the IVB app
innsbruck.note: The Hungerburg funicular and Nordkette cable car go from the centre to the mountains.

graz.pay: Tickets from machines on trams and at stops, or the Graz Linien app
graz.note: Funicular up the Schlossberg castle hill.

krakow.pay: Ticket machines on board and at stops take contactless cards; or the Jakdojade app

warsaw.pay: Ticket machines on board and at stops take contactless cards; or the Jakdojade app

gdansk.pay: Ticket machines on board take contactless cards; or the Jakdojade app
gdansk.note: SKM suburban trains link Gdańsk, Sopot and Gdynia.

wroclaw.pay: Ticket machines on board take contactless cards; or the Jakdojade app

zakopane.note: Private minibuses go to the trailheads; cable car up Kasprowy Wierch (book ahead).

poznan.pay: Ticket machines take contactless cards; or the Jakdojade app

klaipeda.note: Ferry to the Curonian Spit, then buses to Nida.
klaipeda.rentalNote: Bikes on the Curonian Spit cycle path to Nida.

riga.pay: E-tickets from machines and kiosks, or the Mobilly app

sigulda.note: Cable car across the Gauja valley; trails and castles are walkable.
sigulda.rentalNote: Mountain bikes for the Gauja valley trails.

tallinn.pay: QR tickets in the official app, or the Ühiskaart travel card

tartu.rentalNote: Tartu’s smart bike share includes e-bikes.

stpetersburg.pay: Podorozhnik card or tokens, bought with cash; foreign bank cards don't work
stpetersburg.note: Metro signs are also in English. Bridges open at night in summer: plan around them.
stpetersburg.rentalNote: Apps need a Russian bank card, so rentals are hard for foreign visitors.

moscow.pay: Troika card, bought with cash at metro ticket desks; foreign bank cards don't work
moscow.note: Metro announcements and signs are also in English.
moscow.rentalNote: Apps need a Russian bank card, so rentals are hard for foreign visitors.

kazan.pay: Cash or a local transport card; foreign bank cards don't work
kazan.rentalNote: Apps need a Russian bank card, so rentals are hard for foreign visitors.

taipei.pay: EasyCard (sold at MRT stations and convenience stores; also works in shops)
taipei.note: The MRT is spotless and signed in English; YouBike stations are everywhere.

tainan.note: Buses are infrequent: most visitors use YouBike, scooters or taxis.

kaohsiung.note: Ferry to Cijin Island; light rail around the harbour.

hualien.note: Reach Taroko Gorge by tourist bus, taxi tour or scooter.

tokyo.pay: Suica or PASMO card (also on iPhone); paper tickets at machines
tokyo.note: Trains stop around midnight: plan the last train home.

hakone.pay: Hakone Free Pass covers the loop
hakone.note: Classic loop: mountain train, cable car, ropeway and pirate-ship lake cruise.

kyoto.note: Buses get very crowded; a rental bike is often easier.

nara.note: Main sights are within walking distance of the stations.

hiroshima.note: Trams to the Peace Park; train + ferry to Miyajima.

kanazawa.rentalNote: Machi-nori bike share covers the old districts.

takayama.note: Small, walkable old town; buses to Shirakawa-go.

fukuoka.pay: IC card (Hayakaken, Suica and others work)

sapporo.pay: IC card (SAPICA, Suica and others work)

bangkok.pay: Rabbit card or single tickets on the BTS Skytrain; contactless bank cards on the MRT
bangkok.note: Chao Phraya river boats are cheap and avoid traffic.

ayutthaya.note: Rent a bike or hire a tuk-tuk to tour the temple ruins.

kanchanaburi.note: Death Railway trains run to Nam Tok; buses to Erawan Falls.

chiangmai.pay: Cash to the red songthaew trucks (shared, flag one down)
chiangmai.note: The old city is walkable; Grab and Bolt work well.

pai.note: Most travellers rent a scooter: ride carefully on the mountain roads.

krabi.note: Longtail boats to Railay and the islands from Ao Nang.

phuket.note: Taxis are expensive and rarely metered: use Grab or Bolt.

kohsamui.note: Shared songthaews around the island; ferries to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao.

hanoi.note: Grab motorbike taxis are the quickest way around.

sapa.note: Trek to villages with a local guide; motorbike taxis for longer trips.

halong.note: Most visitors arrive with a bay cruise that includes transfers.

ninhbinh.note: Rent a bike or scooter to reach Tam Coc and Trang An.

hue.note: Rent a bike or hire a driver for the royal tombs.

hoian.note: The old town is car-free; cycle to An Bang beach.

hcmc.note: Metro line 1 opened in late 2024; Grab bikes are the easiest way around.

kualalumpur.pay: Touch 'n Go card or single tokens
kualalumpur.note: Free GoKL city buses loop the centre.

georgetown.note: Free CAT shuttle bus in the heritage area; ferry to Butterworth.

cameronhighlands.note: Tours or taxis to the tea plantations.

langkawi.note: No real public transport: rent a car or scooter, or use Grab.

singapore.pay: Tap a contactless bank card or phone on the MRT and buses
singapore.note: Signs are in English; trains are frequent and air-conditioned.

phnompenh.note: Tuk-tuks through PassApp or Grab are the easy option.

siemreap.note: Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day to tour Angkor, or cycle.

battambang.note: Bamboo train and countryside by tuk-tuk or bike.

kampot.note: Rent a scooter for Bokor Mountain and the pepper farms.
